title: [finding] Family dispatch: member label writes are not atomic with the head's, and a member left on `pm:queue` while dispatched is invisible to every existing patrol row
body:
Filed unassigned by the skills execution seat at shift end (session `session_01JANH3y7qe3MD8aLaLXci8N`, 2026-08-26/27). Mechanizable class — the disposition is a patrol row, ⛔ not prose. Grading is the lane's.

## The shape, measured on this seat's own error

A family dispatch flips N cards in N separate label writes. There is no mechanism that ties them together, so a partial run is possible and produced no signal: in a 3-card fold this seat wrote 2 of the 3, leaving one member carrying a **member-pointer comment naming the chain head** while its label still read `pm:queue`.

That combination is a lie in the dispatchable direction — the queue label says "free to claim" about a card already inside someone's in-flight fold. It survived until an unrelated recovery happened to touch the card. ⛔ Not asserted: that anyone acted on it. Nobody did. The finding is that nothing would have said so.

## Why no existing reading catches it

- The half-state patrol's rows key on `assignee` / label / claim-comment pairings **on one card**; this card had no assignee and a consistent-looking `pm:queue`, so it is clean by every per-card predicate.
- The fold's own record lives in the chain head's claim comment — prose, on another card. Nothing joins the two.
- The seat's in-flight ledger is the seat post, which lists the fold by its head.

## Disposition (patrol row candidate, report-only)

A card whose latest comment is a family-dispatch member pointer (or which is named as a member in a live `Claim:` on another open card) but which does not carry `pm:dispatched` — surfaced as patrol input, never a verdict. Both halves are already GitHub-side readings the patrol makes; the join is the new part. Bounded by the open-`pm:dispatched` population, which is small and already swept.

Cheaper alternative worth pricing against it: require the fold's label writes to be verified by a read-back of **every** member before the dispatch launches (a discipline line, no new machinery) — weaker, because it depends on the seat that just proved it can miss one.
